outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: AI and enterprise software, led by Palantir, ServiceNow, and Salesforce
strongest.reason: Palantir extended its post-earnings surge on 93% year-on-year revenue growth, ServiceNow rallied after AI annual contract value crossed $1 billion for the first time, and the broader enterprise-software rebound continues to lift Salesforce and Adobe alongside them

strongest.area: Cybersecurity, led by CrowdStrike and NetApp
strongest.reason: CrowdStrike and NetApp both jumped as the sector continues decoupling from broader software on demand for AI-capable security platforms, with enterprises reportedly treating cybersecurity budgets as largely immune to AI-driven cuts elsewhere in IT

weakest.reason: the stock fell another 10.7% as its slide since Johnson & Johnson's FDA-cleared Ottava platform — its first direct rival to da Vinci — continues to deepen rather than stabilize

weakest.area: Select chip and picks-and-shovels names, particularly Arm, ASML, and Ouster
weakest.reason: these three pulled back even as the broader semiconductor complex found buyers after last week's AI-trade selloff, suggesting the rebound has been uneven rather than sector-wide

outlook.nextStep: The chip sector's early stabilization after last week's steep selloff, alongside Palantir's and ServiceNow's earnings-driven strength, is worth a closer look as markets reopen this week. The Intuitive Surgical competitive story and the crypto market's CLARITY Act delay are more structural and event-driven, and are probably better watched for follow-through than acted on immediately.

signals.title: Fed holds rates steady for a fifth meeting with three dissents favoring a hike
signals.body: The FOMC kept the federal funds target range at 3.50%-3.75% at its July 29 meeting, but three regional presidents dissented in favor of a 25bp hike, leaving the door open to tightening in September. Core PCE inflation has accelerated from 3.0% in December to 3.3% in June, keeping the Fed's path genuinely split heading into its September 15-16 meeting.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how the inflation-vs-labor-market tension resolves before September

signals.title: Chip stocks find buyers after last week's AI-trade selloff shook out
signals.body: After a selloff that briefly wiped over $1 trillion from chip-sector market caps, leveraged semiconductor ETFs jumped more than 5% as buyers returned. Global chip sales hit $403.3 billion in Q2, up 35.1% from Q1, and full-year 2026 sales are on pace to top $1.5 trillion — but the rebound has been uneven, with Arm and ASML still lagging even as Nvidia and Taiwan Semiconductor firmed.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this stabilization broadens or stays concentrated in a handful of names

signals.title: Hyperscaler capex commitments continue anchoring the AI-buildout narrative
signals.body: The five largest US cloud and AI infrastructure providers remain committed to $660-690 billion in 2026 capital expenditure, nearly double 2025 levels. Oracle continues to hold its recent jump on the Google Cloud AI partnership, while Microsoft and Amazon trade closer to flat as the broader capex story stays intact.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether capex acceleration keeps translating into stock performance into Q3 earnings

signals.title: Intuitive Surgical's slide deepens as J&J's Ottava threat weighs further
signals.body: Intuitive Surgical fell roughly 10.7% as the competitive overhang from Johnson & Johnson's FDA-cleared Ottava robotic surgery platform — its first direct challenger in soft-tissue robotic surgery, with an immediate US rollout planned — continues to build rather than fade. Meanwhile Hong Kong- and China-listed humanoid-robotics names, including UBTECH, extended a broad regional rally.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how much further this repricing has to run versus how much is already reflected

signals.title: Palantir and ServiceNow lead a broadening earnings-driven software rally
signals.body: Palantir extended its post-earnings surge (93% year-on-year revenue growth) and ServiceNow rallied after AI annual contract value crossed $1 billion for the first time, with Salesforce and Adobe also participating in a broader enterprise-software rebound that now looks less concentrated than it did a few weeks ago.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this breadth holds or narrows back to a handful of names

signals.title: Senate shelves the CLARITY Act ahead of August recess
signals.body: The US Senate set aside the CLARITY Act, a key piece of crypto market-structure legislation, ahead of its August recess, removing a near-term regulatory catalyst. Bitcoin and ethereum have held relatively steady near recent levels despite the delay and softer-than-expected jobs data.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now on near-term crypto-regulation catalysts until the legislation resurfaces

signals.title: Cybersecurity spending stays insulated as budgets shift away from other enterprise IT
signals.body: A recent survey found 0% of IT leaders identified cybersecurity as a candidate for budget cuts even as AI-driven reallocation sweeps through other enterprise software categories, helping explain why CrowdStrike and NetApp both jumped sharply while broader enterprise software stayed more mixed.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the sector's budget insulation looks structural rather than one-quarter noise
